question: Light of frequency less than the threshold frequency of a metal surface is made very intense. Will photoelectrons be emitted? Justify your answer.

options.A:
No. When $
u<
u_0$, each photon has energy $h
u<\phi_0$, insufficient to eject an electron. Increasing intensity adds more such photons but does not increase the energy of each photon.
options.B: Yes. Very high intensity makes the energy of each photon exceed the work function.
options.C: Yes, but only after a time delay because intensity alone increases photon frequency.
options.D: No, because intense light has zero photons.
